metadata.title: Dice Roll Frequency
metadata.description: Roll a die 1000 times with the random module and tally the sixes into a dict.

instructions.main: Roll a fair die 1000 times with `random.randint(1, 6)`, tally every face into the dict `counts`, and report how many sixes you rolled in the variable `sixes`.
steps: Import the module and seed ONCE before the loop: `import random` then `random.seed(42)` — the seed makes the experiment reproducible.
Finish with `sixes = counts.get(6, 0)` and `print(sixes)` — with this seed you roll 175 sixes.

hints.message: Start with `import random`, seed once, build `counts = {}`, then loop `for _ in range(1000):` tallying each roll.

`random.seed(...)` belongs OUTSIDE the loop — reseeding every roll restarts the generator each time, so you draw the same face 1000 times and `sixes` collapses to 0 (or 1000). Seed once before the loop.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: You seeded once, rolled 1000 times, and tallied the sixes correctly.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Roll the die with the standard library: `import random` and `random.randint(1, 6)`.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: counts is a dict of face to tally.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Store the tallies in a dict named `counts` — `counts = {}`, then `counts[roll] = counts.get(roll, 0) + 1`.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: sixes holds a plausible count above 100.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: `sixes` must be an int greater than 100 — after 1000 genuine (never reseeded) rolls you should count roughly one six in six rolls. Use `sixes = counts.get(6, 0)`.
